[spoiler=From the neighboring Baiame to the distant Mauru and Inuktut.]
A couple of years after the Golden War in 997AD and the Great Joining in 1000 AD Nordiheim would once more find itself with the time and resources to look outside its borders once more as well as the larger world around them.
While the interaction and dealings with the Golden nobles had given the Nordiheimians some exposure to the wider world outside of their own borders it also informed them of how little they actually knew of other nations and peoples out there and how badly outdated the small amount of information they did have was.

While some information was gained from the Golden nobles and their own archives most scholars agreed that it was not entirely reliable and suffered from the prejudice that those nobles had towards anyone that they saw as inferior to themself, as such the council would create and fund several diplomatic and exploratory missions to both potentially expand Nordiheims reach and knowledge of the lands around them and the landmass of Argo that they called home.
[i](Argo is the ancient name used by the Nordiheimians for the continent before Argos became the universally accepted name for it.)[/i] 

The first of these missions started around 1030 AD and would over the next 200 years or so would bring Nordiheim a great amount of knowledge and understanding of world around them, especially regarding the continents of Argos and the two Shamats, but would reveal the existence of Nordiheim to other nations and peoples be it for good or bad.
There were however 2 events in particular that were the most noteworthy to Nordiheimian history in the first 100 years of its golden age, the further joining of Aboriginal tribes into the Aboria region and providing military protection to distant Argossian peoples, in both cases it would lead to Nordiheim growing in size, though at different speeds.

[b][u]The joining of Irohgrad and the brother tribes of Baiame[/u][/b]

The first missions that the Nordiheimians conducted outwardly were diplomatic ones to the west of Aboria, specifically to the tribes of Dati and Baiame.
While the diplomatic talks with the tribes of Dati did not end with the same type of success that had been achieved with Irohgrad in the past as the tribes saw the Nordiheimians as too aggressive, something that the now retired Chief Yarramundi had given them a friendly warning about as the Dati tribes were known to be of a  pacifist nature, they still managed to create a connection that would over the years be used for trade and settling disagreements. The talks with the tribes of Baiame would have much better results for the Nordiheimians on the other hand.

The tribes of Baiame lived in the lands directly south from the Dati tribes, a land that was less green and covered in tall yellow grass that could be seen stretching all the way until it met the foot of the red wall mountain.
The Nordiheimians would travel to the village of Popanig where the chiefs of all the tribes of Baiame would gather and meet them for talks about whether they would join the Aboria region, where their brother people of Iroh lived, as a new part of a wider Nordiheim nation.

While the talks would take weeks, as the gathered chiefs wanted to be certain that they and their people got more from a joining then they lost, with many questions and inquiries about what Nordiheim was and what they stood for, the knowledge shared did not just go one way.
The Nordiheimians would learn many things about the different tribes and clans that the Baiame was made up of, there was the three tribes of Popa, Kora and Kurda and their villages that essentially was the largest voice and power among them as they counted almost two-thirds of the people as their own.

The Popa of Popanig village, the village were the talks was taking place, was built atop a large and ancient underground lake which provided water to many of the tribes of the Baiame, this also allowed them to keep a herd of kangaroos that provided them with meat for both food and trade.

The Kora tribe of Korayn village for their part had a salt mine similar to the Ngura village that was connected to Irohgrad, though Korayn was close to the foot of Red Wall mountain and as such far away from Ngura.

Meanwhile the Kardu tribe of Kardu Kungka village had only one resource that allowed them to be relevant, which was the incredible skill of their people in both hunting and treating leather, two groups of skills that went well together.

Lastly the Nordiheimians learned of one small tribe called the Nagoio who made almost all trinkets and art for religious purposes and could also be said to be the home of many spirit talkers, the priests of their religion.
Used in much of the religious pieces was a brilliant red rock which they called Uluru, mined from the rocky land they called home, and while its shape and cut was somewhat crude since they did not have access to the same quality of tools that Nordiheimians had it was still beautifully incorporated into the art and decorations it was used in.
One of the Vestlandian scholars that was part of the Nordiheimian diplomatic team pointed out that the red rock matched the description of a gemstone called a ruby which was a valuable gemstone, this was conveyed honestly to the gathered chiefs by the man.
While some members of the Nordiheimian diplomatic team found it slightly foolish to just reveal such valuable information to the Baiame they also knew that honesty had usually produced the best results in the past when dealing with any of the Aboriginal peoples and as such did not try to prevent it.

The chieftains of the Baiame not only found that the Nordiheimians negotiated in good faith with them but also that they showed them honesty, as such they felt that their demands regarding trade, hunting rights and equal status within Nordiheim could be agreed upon with enough fairness that they would gain more than enough to find joining the nation as a part of the Aboria region was to their people's benefit.

As such the negotiations with the tribes of Baiame arrived smoothly at an agreement between them and the Nordiheimians.
By the next year the integration would fully start up with the people of the Baiame tribes going through an enumeration so that they could be registered in the Aborian Census. Propper roads would also be made in their land to more easily connect them with the rest of the region including a great cobblestone road that connected the three main villages of Popanig, Korayn and Kardu Kungka to not only connect them to each other but also the main road going between Irohgrad and the national capitol Midgard.

Trade would start to flow between the Baiame and the rest of Nordiehim with dried meat, salt, raw rubies and good leather being their first trade goods in return for better tools, dried fruits, camels and metals.The access to better tools in particular would allow the Baiame tribes to refine their crafts over time to make not only better goods but also new ones like the spiritual statuettes and items which would become the speciality of the Nagoio tribe in the future.
By August of 1035 AD the land of the Baiame tribes would become integrated enough that they would officially become part of Nordiheim and the region of Aboria.

[b][u]Exploring the coast and meeting the Mauru.[/u][/b]
In 1030 AD Nordiheim would send two exploration fleets, the western and eastern exploration fleets, to map out the coast of their continent, sending one in each direction, to see if there were other nations or peoples of significant size or importance that they could potentially start up relations and trade with.
While the eastern exploration fleets eastwards journey down the eastern coast of Argo would not bring back much information that would be exiting to history books, the western exploration fleet that sailed down the western coast of the continent would eventually bring back much more interesting news in the form of new friends that would after centuries of friendship and close diplomatic relations become part of Nordiheim.

The western exploration fleet that was sent to explore the western coast of Argos, under the command of Nordlandian captain Siguri Kwesisen would in the beginning not really encounter anything truly special as they would for the most part just make minor diplomatic contact with coastal tribes for potential future contact and trade as well as making a map of the coast.
The first observation of note happened when the fleet sailed southwards along the wider western coast as the log book of the expedition claims to have seen humanoid beings that seemed to be humans mixed with animals. Half the crew of the expedition seem to have become convinced that the western land might be cursed and that the people that they spotted were humans that had been merged with animals through dark arts or corruption of the soul.
While Captain Siguri himself called the claim [i]Strunpraw kabisa[/i] ((Compleat nonsense)) he could not go against the wishes of so many of the fleet's crew and as such did not attempt any kind of contact with the observed beings to prevent the loss of morale or the threat of potential mutinies that could break out if he tried to initiate contact.

It was not until they had passed most of the western coast and came to where the continent started taking a more south-eastern direction that the exploration fleet would eventually come in contact with a new group of people that would become part of Nordiheims future.
While observing the many pods of whales that they had discovered in the waters off the south-westernmost coast of mainland Argos, that they were making observations and notations about for potential future whale hunting, the fleets lookouts would start reporting that they had observed what looked to be smaller ships making landfall on the nearby coast as well as smoke starting to rise from what seemed to be a large coastal village that they had planned to make contact with ones they were finished documenting the whales. To determine the nature of this observed attack the fleet, made up of 5 large Sea Drake ships that had originaly been made for war, would quickly sail towards the village so that they could find out if this was an action of war between two peoples or something more savage.

As they got close enough to see what was happening in more detail it quickly became apparent that the group attacking the village were most likely raiders of some sort based on their rag tag composition of their fleet and their disorganized reaction when they finally spotted their fleet, with ships that looked like they had been made by many different peoples and symbols on their sails and flags depicting weapons of war and predatory animals colored red or black 
While Captain Siguri had been asked by the council back home to try and avoid getting directly involved in any conflicts it did not feel right to him to simply leave this village to its fate, as such he ordered the fleet under his command to immediately get into formation and informed the other captains sail to the defence of the coastal village declaring that he would personally take the responsibility of the outcome of this action.

Despite having fewer ships and men then the group attacking the village it would not be too difficult to achieve victory against them. Half of their ships laid at the shore with their crews fully disembarked and the other half  was caught in a disarray that left them unable to take advantage of their greater numbers.
The Sea Drake ships of the Nordiheimians were larger than their opponents by quite a bit and their ramming attacks would nearly rip the smaller ships in half with their powerful rostrums.
Also on land when the Nordiheimians made landfall to take care of the raiders they found victory easy as many of the Nordiheimians were veterans from the Golden War while the raiders lacked proper discipline and had weapons and armor that were as rag tag as their ships, and it didnt help them that some of the villages warriors were still standing leaving them fighting on two fronts.
It did not take long before the raiders were either dead or captured with only 4 ships having escaped as they had used their speed and maneuverability, their only advantages, to run away and avoid the fate of their fellow raiders.

After the raiders had been dealt with the leader of the village would approach the Nordiheimians with careful gratitude to not only thank them for the help but also to figure out what the price of this aid might be. When Captain Siguri meets with the village leader and tells him that all that they would want is the potential for friendship and trade the village leader is intrigued and introduces himself as Koa Te Ariki of Whangiri village and tells Siguri that the Mauru people will happily welcome a fellow warrior people with friendship when they have already proven that they will provide aid to those that are unfairly attacked by others.
Unfortunately he also says that on the matter of trade they can not offer much as long as the wider raider treat still remains as the raiding party that attacked their village was only smaller part of a much larger group led by a cowardly man that fancies himself a king of the southern sea, or Sea King, that aims to lay all the peoples on the southern coast as his vassals or tributaries, this especially applies to themself, the Mauru, as their lands was the home of several types of trees that was good for ship building such as the Gum trees and the Blackwood.

To Captain Siguri's initial surprise he finds that when he asks about these Gum and Blackwood trees Koa Te Ariki not only answers his questions but even lead him to a nearby forest of Gum trees so that he and some of his crew can see and inspect the trees and some of their canoe ships that they had hidden from the raiders that was made from said wood. The ship carpenters that came with Siguri confirmed that the wood seemed to indeed be well suited for use in ship construction after having studied the wood of the trees and the canoe ships.
Siguri quickly realized why village leader Koa Te Ariki was so willing to show this to him and his men, he was giving showing them why it could be in Nordiheims interest to not only see them as a potentially valuable trade partner but also give them a reason to see the Sea King and his raiders as an enemy that was worth getting rid of and honestly it would probably work if he relayed this information to the council back home, Nordiheim might have lumber for ship building but it was not as good quality as what the Mauru had.
His musings on this matter was interrupted though as a messenger from the village came running to tell his leader that a Mauru war band had arrived in the village and the leader of the war band was demanding to know who the strangers (Nordiheimians) were and what exactly had happened regarding the raiders, Koa Te Ariki seemed rather surprised about this and explained that it usually took a war band longer to reach them then this and he had not expected them to come this quickly.

When Captain Siguri and Koa Te Ariki arrived back to the village they would find out that the war band was led by none other than the High Chief of the Mauru himself. After having the situation explained to him and that the strangers had helped them against the raiders the high chief introduced himself as Rangi Te Maia Manaia and thanked the Nordiheimians for aiding the people of Mauru in their defence of their village, Rangi then invited Captain Siguri and the captains of the four other Nordiheimian ships in a show of trust to join him and other important Mauru that had joined his war band for discussion about the raiders and talks of potential negotiations between their two peoples to not only come to a better understanding of each other but perhaps something more.

Through the talks Siguri and the other Nordiheimians learned more about the situation regarding the raiders and the Mauru position in it all.
They learned that the reason that the warband had managed to get to the village so quickly was because they had traveled as quickly as they were able to in the hopes that they would reach it fast enough to still engage the raiders before they had the time to loot all that they wanted and depart on their ships and since they had arrived a whole day faster than any Mauru warband had before this could have potentially have happened if the Nordiheimians had not decided to aid the village.
The reason Rangi had tried to achieve this was because he wished to gain a victory against the raiders of the Sea King as they were unable to gather all their warriors and set sail to confront the Sea Kings forces directly, the many ships that the Mauru had used to have had been heavily reduced by the first raids that had hit them about 3 years ago and left them unable to harvest the bounty of the ocean which was their people's main source of food even inland through salted and dried sea food, and any time they had made new canoes to try and fish they had always been attacked by the raiders before they could acquire the decisive amount of food they would need to feed both their people and a proper army to try and defeat the Sea King at his base of operation.  Losing their ability to properly fish was the main root of why they were being raided yet unable to strike back as they already knew where the Sea King had his main base of operation.
Rangi would then, without any pretense, give a message to Captain Siguri that he was to deliver to his peoples leaders which was both a plea for help and an offer to the Nordiheimian, if they would help them end this threat to the future of the Mauru people then they would not only trade freely with them but even allow them access to their land in ways that had been allowed to anyone else.
When one of the other Nordiheimian captains asked about the possibility of setting up a whaling operation on the Maurus coast Rangi confirmed that it was something they would be willing to allow as long as they respected the great sea beasts death by not wasting the bounty of its body something the Nordiheimians did not believe would become a problem.

When the talks was finished and the meeting ended Captain Siguri would tell Rangi and the other assembled Mauru that it would take some time for them to travel home and relay their message asking for aid and as such they would have to survive another year of raids before they would be able to come back and give them the answer their council would give, Rangi replied with confidence that his people would be able to do this with the other Mauru speaking in agreement.
Siguri and the rest of the Nordiheimians would depart the following morning after loading some gum tree lumber on two of their ships and set sail directly towards the closest Nordiheimian port in the Ostland region, thankfully the voyage would be an uneventful one with decent winds in their favor allowing them to return in good time. Once they laid anchor at the port town of Berghavn a message was immediately sent to the council of Nordiheim by bird informing them that the western exploration fleet had returned sooner than expected and had brought an important message from the chiefdom that they had made contact with on their journey.

When the council met with Captain Siguri and his fellow captains in Ostland's regional capital of Hadanger it did not take too long for a consensus to be reached by them, since the faster they decided the better the result would potentially be, the prospect of gaining access to the special lumber that the Mauru possessed was of great value as the ship builders they quickly gathered confirmed that the gum wood that had been brought was indeed superior to the wood that they already used.
It was also in the opinion of the minister of war a great opportunity to make use of the many warships and veteran warriors that they still had from the Golden War and would just wither away to idleness if not used soon, as such a fleet of 15 Sea Serpent war ships and 3 large Sea Dragon ships to carry extra men and cargo would be gathered together with the warriors and supplies needed over the the course of about one month before this new fleet under the command of Captain Siguri would set sail to the land of the Mauru to help them take care of the Sea King and his raiders.

When Captain Siguri once more arrived at Whangiri village with the large Nordiheimian fleet roughly one year after he left to find the Mauru still holding their ground against the raiders who had continued the raids on their coastal villages after they had left.
High chief Rangi Te Maia Manaia did not need much time to gather his peoples warriors and what ships that they had hidden away from the raiders as he had already sent calls for them to gather in anticipation of the Nordiheimians accepting his offer, a calculated gamble he had done, and soon the Mauru joined the Nordiheimians with a fleet of their own made up of smaller ships and canoe ships and leading the large fleet towards where they knew the Sea King had made his base.

The battle that would follow when the combined Nordiheimian and Mauru fleet attacked the base of the infamous Sea King is not greatly covered in modern history books with the exception of some key details.
The Sea Kings base was made in the bay of an island where a large village made of old ships and drift wood was situated with the piers of its harbor being made out of mostly old long trade and cargo ships whose masts had been chopped down to make them flat.
The large fleet of Nordiheimians and Mauru attacked the Sea Kings base during the night by using the villages own night lights as their guide to gain the advantage of surprise, by the time the raiders realized that they were being attacked the fleet had already secured the mouth of the bay and essentially made it impossible for the raiders to sail out in their nimble ships, this allowed Mauru warriors and the old Nordiheimian veterans that was looking for a final battle to secure their entry into Valhalla to land while the raiders were still disorganized and their organization in chaos. Most of the raiders could in fact not offer more resistance than a militia at best with the only exception being the Sea King, which the few sources that describe him paint him as a muscular man as large as a Norse of old with a long obsidian mane of hair, and his core group of 100 veteran raiders that was by far the most competent and experienced men under his command with his right and left hand men, Xivan the black and Jarajara the marauder, commanding them on his behalf with surprising efficiency.
But this did not change the outcome for the Sea King and his army of raiders as they would all either be slain, captured or flee deeper into the island's interior with the Sea King himself being killed in a duel with Rangi himself which led to the morale of the last raiders collapsing.
With the Sea King and the raider threat ended the Nordiheimian and Mauru would loot the raider village off its more valuable items before setting sail back home, though some warriors would claim that it felt like they were being watched during the looting it was assumed that it most likely was left over raiders watching them from afar that had escaped the slaughter and was now hiding in the rocky hill nearby and as such not a problem worth dealing with.

When the large fleet returned to the village of Whangiri they were met with jubilation when the villagers understood that they had been successful in taking out the raider threat and preparations for a feast were quickly started.
Though since food were a bit of a problem the Nordiheimians not only offered to share of their own supplies, as they had brought more than they needed, but also sent some of their ships out to capture a whale from a pod that had been spotted just off the coast so that there would be no lack of food as nearby villages were also coming to celebrate the end of the raids.
The feast that took place a few days later was perhaps not the largest that the Nordiheimians had ever seen but it still lasted for a few days, with both foods that familiar to them and food that they had never tasted before but found to be to their taste, and it was a feast that they could easily enjoy as the Mauru people treated them well as they saw them as fellow warriors that had both aided them and proven their skill in battle while shoulder-to-shoulder with their own warriors.

When the victory feast came to a close the chiefs of the Mauru together with their high chief sat down with Captain Siguri and other Nordiheimian commanders and two diplomats that had joined the Nordiheimina fleet just for this part to put the full agreement between their two people on parchment.
Mauru would be given protection through a one-way defensive pact were Nordiheim would come to their defence if they were attacked but the Mauru was not bound to do the same in return, in return Nordiheim would be given preferential trade rights, the permission to do whaling of their coast with a whaling station at a location of their choice as well as  the permission to turn a coastal village into a proper port with a shipyard that could handle their much larger ships, the village of Whangiri was chosen after chief Koa Te Ariki invited the Nordiheimians to chose his village by declaring that its inhabitants would gladly cooperate with them.
With this the foundation that would eventually bring the Mauru into the fold of Nordiheim had been laid.

[b][u]The inclusion of the Bascover islands and how Nordiheim gained another region.[/u][/b]
As the Nordiheimians built up the port and the facilities that they needed in the village of Whengiri they would not only gain a place that would extend the reach of their nations in matters of trade and influence but also create the foundations that would turn the village into the first proper Mauru city that would be the center of their peoples technological and cultural evolution as it would become their most important trade port and a place that they would be able to make the largest of their particular canoe ships for fishing and transport of goods and people.

The whaling station that the Nordiheimians would make in the same village would also end up creating a flow of food that would free up the people there to take up work and crafts that they had not been able to when every man had been needed to catch enough fish for people to eat, as a result the type and amount of goods that they could create not only for them self but also trade would increase as something akin to primitive industry would start to take form allowing them to trade more than simply raw resources.

As the Mauru developed as a people they would solidify how they governed their land and create a government inspired by the Nordiheimian council as well as other governments that they learned about, each village area chose one elder and a chief that would represent them in a senate were the position of High Chief became the executive head of state, they also took the name Hawaiki for their little nation.

This emerging prosperity during the next two centuries would prompt the Mauru explore the sea and islands to their far south which included the large island that had been the place of the Sea Kings base of operation, while they originally had thought that the islands was uninhabited they would be surprised by the discovery that this was not the case and that there had actually been people living the large island for some time even long before the Sea King had made his base there who called themself the Inuktut.
When the Mauru initiated contact with the Inuktut they initially reacted rather defensively to towards them until they realized who they actually were and their attitude changed completely to a very friendly one that was initially a bit surprising to the Mauru, the reason became clear after they shared their history and that the reason they were so welcoming toward them was because their people had been forced to serve the Sea King and when the Mauru had destroyed his raider army and killed him and his commanders they had also freed them.

The Inuktut had been forced by the Sea King to provide him with supplies and forced labor under the threat of death and violence if they did not obey and so had been overjoyed when the Mauru had arrived with the large fleet and laid waste to the Sea King and his raider army, but they also apologised for not making contact with them after the Sea Kings fall as their people had instead kept themself hidden as they were fearful of strong they were for being able to defeat their oppressor, by the time they had decided to try and make contact with them they found that the Mauru warriors had already left.

As the two peoples talked on and learned about each other, including the fact that the large island and the islands to the east of it were more of the Inuktut lived was collectively called Bascover by the Inuktut, it started becoming apparent to the Mauru that the Inuktut did not know about the Nordiheimians and their involvement in the fight against the Sea King as they started asking them about the largest ships that had been part of the fleet back then and how they could make such large en fearsome ships. While the Inuktut was at first surprised that another people had not only helped face the Sea King but that they had also been the ones that had made it possible they would quickly ask the Mauru to introduce them to these Nordiheimians so that they could properly thank them and offer them their gratitude, something that the Mauru had no problem arranging.

The Nordiheimians and the Inuktut would official meet a year later in 1233 AD, the group of diplomatic representatives that had been sent by the Nordiheimian council was just as surprised as the Mauru had been when they learned about the Inuktut and how they had been freed when Nordiheim had helped against the Sea King.
When the three peoples had a long talk to share their histories and cultures with each other the subject of the protection that the Nordiheimians provided the Mauru naturally came up when the Mauru and Inuktut started mentioning that they had started discussing the possibility of their two peoples joining together as one nation for mutual protection and benefits as they had found that they worked rather well together with their individual expertise being helpful to the other and asked if the Bascover islands could also become protected by the Nordiheimians.
While the Nordiheimian diplomats could not think of a reason to really reject this as it would increase the range of their ship in the area it did not hurt that the Inuktut presented them with some of the things that they could trade with them which included many different herbs, a strange plant they called Aloe and a sweet drink they called Agave juice, as such the Nordiheimians agreed to widen their protection to also include the islands of the Inuktut.
As a result of this the Mauru and Inuktut would have a great meeting of leaders after the meeting with the Nordiheimians and declare themself two people joined as one as they expanded and evolved the government that the Mauru had already made into essentially a republic were they had the same amount of representatives and the High Chief position could be filled by a worthy person from either people.
  
While the Mauru and Inuktut would experience a rather long period of peace and prosperity as one nation as the Nordiheimians would shield and protect them from threats, with only the Mauru facing some minor conflicts and skirmishes with other neighboring tribes and roaming war bands of what the Mauru called beast men, this period would finally come to an abrupt and bloody end in the early 20th century during the Great War.

The Republic of Hawaiki & Bascover as it would be called at the time would at the start of the war decide to take a neutral stance towards the conflict which would continue even after Nordiheim became an active participant one year later in 1915, with the Nordiheimans respectfully removing the local navy they had stationed in the port city of Whengiri so that its presence did not cause the small nations neutrality to be endangered or questioned.
Unfortunately for the Mauru and the Inuktut they would become the target of an Imperial League member who saw their small republic as an easy target to increase their overseas holdings and claim an easy conquest to increase their prestige among the other league members through the use of a casus belli that was thin at best or fabricated nonsense at worst as it was entirely based on their claim that the republic of Hawaiki & Bascover was not actually an independent nation that was benefiting from protection from a larger nation but actualy just an extension of Nordiheim masquerading as some sort of protectorate and as such a threat to the league that needed to be dealt with.

The declaration of war on small republic would happen on the 4th of July 1917 and would see Mauru and Inuktut losing the fight on the sea as their navy mostly consisted of smaller gun boats as they had not needed a large navy with Nordiheim protecting them with theirs for so many centuries, and while the Imperial League nation would successfully land troops on the Hawaiki mainland they would quickly face defeat on that front from a combination of overconfidence, the use of almost entirely green soldiers and conscripts and the surprisingly fast mobilization and response of the Mauru army.
The republic army, which consisted majorly of Mauru people, was far stronger and more competent than the navy had been as not only was that the part of their military that had actually had to face threats to their nation but the Mauru had also kept their warrior culture alive and as such it was seen as a right of passage for any Mauru male to complete military training and serve in the military for those who did not was seen as weak and less reliable, as such the republic military would be able force the enemy army to withdraw in humiliation.

The Imperial League nation would not take this failure well though and would double down on their goal to invade the small republic and would claim that the first invasions failure was simply caused by bad luck and the fierce barbaric way of war that the native Argossian people used which was something they declared would not repel them a second time. But they would make sure that the next invasion army was much better prepared and contained more well trained soldiers as the reputation of their military and nation as a whole could be in danger if they suffered another humiliating defeat against what they saw as inferior natives.
By the time they launched their second invasion attempt though the Imperial League nation would find that the Nordiheimians had come to uphold their ancient promise of protecting the Mauru and Inuktut in full force with both their navy contesting the sea and troops to reinforce the republic army on land.

The battles that followed in the Mauru mainland and islands of the Inuktut would be the bloodiest that Nordiheims military would take part in during the Great War and would at one point see as much as 50% of the republics territory falling under the League nations control, but by the end of the Great War the combined Nordiheimian and republic forces would be in control of almoust 90% of it from many bloody back and forth battles against stubborn League forces that would refuse to abandon republic territory as a matter of pride regardless of how many men they ended throwing into the meat grinder that the invasion gradually turned into.
When the Great War was finally over and peace signed on September the 3rd 1921 Nordiheim had deployed over half a million men to the battlefields of Hawaiki over the course of the war with roughly half of them losing their life there, making it the single most costly battlefront that the Nordiheimians had fought on.

After the war the general sentiment that had emerged among the Mauru and Inuktut peoples was the feeling that they perhaps should join the nation of Nordihiem as a new region as the Nordiheimians had ones more come to their aid when they needed it the most and as such proven that they were a people they could fully trust, this line of thought was especially prevalent among the Mauru people that had fought and bled side-by-side with the Nordiheimian soldiers and the civilians that had lived were the heaviest fighting had taken place during the war.
The fact that the fresh war cemeteries contained more Nordiheimian graves than Mauru and Inuktut ones also made it impossible to not take note of how many of them had died fighting for them.

By 1927 a national vote was done after many debates and public hearings to see what the people of the republic wanted for their future; did they want to remain an independent nation that was protected by Nordiheim or did they see a better future for themself by joining together with them and becoming Nordiheimians themself?
The vote came as significantly in favor of joining together with Nordiheim with 79% in favor and only a small 18% wanting to stay independent.
When the people of Nordiheims several regions learned that they would be joined by new brothers and sisters a celebration that some say was greater than the victory celebration for the Great Wars end was had and the Nordiheimian council happily welcomed the Mauru and Inuktut into the fold.
The only true request that the Mauru and Inuktut had for the council, which the council had no problem agreeing to, was that they be given its own branch within the Nordiheimian military just as Nordland and Olia regions had, this was to ensure that the region could defend itself in case of a surprise war or it being isolated in a conflict, of especial interest was the creation of a proper navy branch that had the capacity to actually defend the somewhat distant region.

The official international announcement of the Republic of Hawaiki & Bascover joining Nordiheim as a new region, which would get the name The region of Hawaiki & Bascover, was made in 1929 AD with the work of full integration already underway.
The speed of this integration was much faster than some had initially thought it would be though, some point to the fact that the Maruu and Inuktut had adopted many of the same governmental and infrastructure choices as Nordiheim over the centuries because of their close diplomatic and economic ties which left less work to do.
As for the Mauru military branch it got its navy HQ in the port city of Whengiri and the army HQ was placed in the now regional capital city of Nulmanla, meanwhile the HQ of the regional airforce would be placed on the largest island of the inuktut near the city of Sinunimak.
